children: EUROPE BEFORE THE BELL: TECH REBOUNDS, ALSTOM SLUMPS
European shares were set for a slightly firmer start on Monday as oil prices fell and US futures rebounded, though midterm elections and more tech earnings could keep markets volatile.
gained 0.1%, while those on the DAX
Nasdaq futures advanced 0.7% after Friday's sharp selloff, with Apple
results due later on Monday and updates from Nvidia, Broadcom and other AI-linked tech heavyweights later this month keeping the earnings spotlight firmly on the sector.
In European premarket trade, AI names led gains, with ASML
slumped 20% before the bell after cutting guidance again and forecasting a €1.5 billion cash outflow. Energy stocks were mostly lower, tracking a more than 3% drop in crude prices.
Later in the week, central banks in Sweden, Britain and Norway meet to decide policy.
